title: McGuffey's First Eclectic Reader
sourceTitle: McGuffey's First Eclectic Reader, Revised Edition
author: William Holmes McGuffey
licenseEvidence: Project Gutenberg eBook #14640: 'Public domain in the USA.' Revised edition first copyrighted 1879 (Van Antwerp, Bragg & Co.); renewals 1896, 1907, and 1920, all before 1930.
description: The classic First Reader takes a beginning reader from “The dog ran” to real little stories about pets, picnics, and brave dogs. Each lesson starts with its new words; you practice them, read the story together, copy a line, and talk about it. The full text is free online.
includes: 61 lessons in 8 units covering all 63 First Reader lessons
Link to the free full text for every lesson
New words and a sound focus for each lesson
Copywork line and a hands-on or narration activity
Review and script (cursive) slate lessons marked in the notes

lessons.title: Lessons I–II: The Dog and the Cat
steps: New words: dog, the, ran, cat, mat, is, on; sound focus: short a, short o, short i; th
Read the lesson aloud together, pointing to each word; then let your child read it alone
Slate work: copy “The cat is on the mat.”
Sound out d-o-g and c-a-t, then change one letter to make log, hat, sat
questions: What did the dog do?
Where is the cat?
lessons.notes: Two very short opening lessons combined into one sitting.

lessons.title: Lesson III: The Man and the Pen
steps: New words: it, his, pen, hand, in, has, man; sound focus: short e; p, h
You read a line, then your child reads it back; finish by reading the whole lesson together
Slate work: copy “The man has a pen.”
Hold a pen in your hand and act out the last two lines
questions: What does the man have?
Where is the pen?

lessons.title: Lesson IV: The Fat Hen
steps: New words: hen, fat, rat, box, big, run, from, can; sound focus: short u; f, b, x
Let your child read the lesson aloud slowly; help only on words they can't sound out
Slate work: copy “The fat hen is on the box.”
Narrate: who is on the box and who ran away?
questions: Where is the fat hen?
What ran from the box?

lessons.title: Lesson V: Rab Has the Hat
steps: New words: Rab, Ann, hat, catch, see; sound focus: ch
Read it once aloud for your child, then have them read it to you (or to a sibling or stuffed animal)
Slate work: copy “See Rab! See Ann!”
Look at the picture: why is Ann running?
questions: What does Rab have?
Who is trying to catch Rab?

lessons.title: Lesson VI: Ann Catches Rab
steps: New words: she, pat, too, now, let, me; sound focus: sh, oo, ow
Read the lesson aloud together, pointing to each word; then let your child read it alone
Slate work: copy “Now Ann can pat Rab.”
Tell how the story from Lesson V ends
questions: Did Ann catch Rab?
What does Ann do to Rab now?

lessons.title: Lesson VII: The Black Hen
steps: New words: Ned, eggs, black, left, fed, nest, them, get, will; sound focus: ck; w
You read a line, then your child reads it back; finish by reading the whole lesson together
Slate work: copy “She is a black hen.”
Count the eggs in the picture
questions: What color is the hen?
Who fed the hen?

lessons.title: Lesson VIII: The Big Black Hat
steps: New words: head, he, Nat, come, with; sound focus: ea as short e (head)
Let your child read the lesson aloud slowly; help only on words they can't sound out
Slate work: copy “Ned has it on his head.”
Play dress-up with a big hat and read the lesson in a 'big man' voice
questions: Who has the black hat on his head?
Who is called to come and see?

lessons.title: Lesson IX: Review
steps: Read the old words at the top quickly, like a game
Slate work: copy “The man has a hat.”
Narrate: what is in the box, and who has the black hat?
questions: Where is the big rat?
What should Nat get?
lessons.notes: Review lesson: the words at the top are old words to practice. Let your child read as independently as possible. Ends with slate work (script) to copy.

lessons.title: Lesson X: Nell and the Eggs
steps: New words: Nell, some, pan, him, yes, do, you, have; sound focus: y as a consonant; v
Read the lesson aloud together, pointing to each word; then let your child read it alone
Slate work: copy “She has a pan with some eggs in it.”
Read it as a conversation, with your child as Nell
questions: What does Nell have?
Who will run to catch Rab?
answers: A pan with some eggs in it

lessons.title: Lesson XI: Jip and the Cart
steps: New words: O, whip, Ben, up, still, sit, if, stand, Jip; sound focus: wh; j
You read a line, then your child reads it back; finish by reading the whole lesson together
Slate work: copy “Get up, Jip!”
Look at the picture: what kind of animal is Jip?
questions: What does Ann want to do?
What must she do first?

lessons.title: Lesson XII: Kitty's Pet Bird
steps: New words: Kitty, nice, sweet, sing, just, hang, cage, then, song, pet, put, not; sound focus: ng; long i (nice)
Let your child read the lesson aloud slowly; help only on words they can't sound out
Slate work: copy “It can sing a sweet song.”
Narrate: why does Kitty hang the cage up?
questions: What can Kitty's pet do?
Why will Kitty hang the cage up?
answers: So the cat can not catch the bird

lessons.title: Lesson XIII: Tom and His Dog
steps: New words: Tom, top, Kitty's, at, back, look, good, doll, think, spot; sound focus: short oo (look, good)
Read it once aloud for your child, then have them read it to you (or to a sibling or stuffed animal)
Slate work: copy “Tom has a big top, too.”
Spin a top if you have one, or talk about the picture
questions: Where is the black spot on the dog?
Where is Tom's top?
answers: On the box with Kitty's doll

lessons.title: Lesson XIV: The Duck on the Pond
steps: New words: sun, we, how, pond, stop, for, go, swim, her, us, hot, duck; sound focus: er (her)
Read the lesson aloud together, pointing to each word; then let your child read it alone
Slate work: copy “Now the duck will swim in the pond.”
Tell what the man fed, and where each animal went
questions: What will the duck do now?
Why don't they stop at the pond?

lessons.title: Lesson XV: Run, Skip, and Jump
steps: New words: John, rock, set, jump, fun, must, may, under, skip, bank, but, touch; sound focus: two-syllable word: un-der
You read a line, then your child reads it back; finish by reading the whole lesson together
Slate work: copy “We must not touch the nest.”
Go outside and run, skip, and jump like the children
questions: Where is the duck's nest?
May they touch the nest?
answers: On the bank, under the rock

lessons.title: Lesson XVI: Review: By the Pond
steps: Read the review in turns, one sentence each
Slate work: copy “The sun has set, and the pond is still.”
Find every name in the lesson and count them
questions: Where is Kitty's doll?
Where does the duck have her nest?
lessons.notes: Review lesson: the words at the top are old words to practice. Let your child read as independently as possible.

lessons.title: Lessons XVII–XVIII: Slate Work
steps: New words: are, ink, moss, this, tub, upset, nut, did, shut, shall, lost, fox, men, met, step, into, hunt, mud; sound focus: two-syllable words: up-set, in-to
Read it once aloud for your child, then have them read it to you (or to a sibling or stuffed animal)
Slate work: copy “Ben upset the tub.”
Choose three short sentences from the two slate pages and copy them neatly
questions: Who upset the tub?
What did Ben lose?
lessons.notes: Lessons XVII and XVIII are script (cursive) slate pages only, so they are combined. Read the script together before copying.

lessons.title: Lesson XIX: The Old Cow
steps: New words: Kate, old, no, grass, dear, likes, be, drink, milk, cow, out, gives; sound focus: long a (Kate)
Read the lesson aloud together, pointing to each word; then let your child read it alone
Slate work: copy “She gives us sweet milk.”
Narrate: why won't the cow come out of the pond?
questions: Where is the old cow?
What does the cow give us?

lessons.title: Lesson XX: Riding on Prince
steps: New words: mamma, large, as, papa, arms, ride, far, barn, both, Prince, trot, your; sound focus: ar (far, barn, arms)
You read a line, then your child reads it back; finish by reading the whole lesson together
Slate work: copy “We are both on Prince.”
Pretend to trot to the barn as you reread it

How far will Prince trot?

lessons.title: Lesson XXI: Fanny's Ball
steps: New words: of, that, toss, fall, well, Fanny, ball, wall, was, pretty, done, what; sound focus: all (ball, wall, fall)
Let your child read the lesson aloud slowly; help only on words they can't sound out
Slate work: copy “That was well done.”
Toss a ball back and forth, reading one line per catch
questions: What does Fanny have?
Where should Fanny toss it next?
answers: To the top of the wall

lessons.title: Lesson XXII: At the Pond with Tom
steps: New words: had, went, call, might, flag, near, swam, swing; sound focus: short a (had, flag, swam)
Read it once aloud for your child, then have them read it to you (or to a sibling or stuffed animal)
Slate work: copy “We fed her.”
Narrate what the girl and Tom did at the pond
questions: What did Tom take to the pond?
Where do they want to go next?

lessons.title: Lesson XXIII: Here Comes the Band
steps: New words: here, band, hear, horse, play, they, pass, where, front, fine, hope, comes; sound focus: hear and here sound alike
Read the lesson aloud together, pointing to each word; then let your child read it alone
Slate work: copy “Here comes the band!”
March around the room like the band
questions: Who is in front of the band?
What do the boys hope?
answers: A large man with a big hat
That the band will stop and play for them

lessons.title: Lesson XXIV: In the Woods
steps: New words: Bess, happy, make, cart, tent, woods, little, very, bed, Robert, gone, draw; sound focus: two-syllable words: hap-py, lit-tle
You read a line, then your child reads it back; finish by reading the whole lesson together
Slate work: copy “Bess and Robert are very happy.”
Build a blanket tent and read the lesson inside it
questions: What does Robert have?
What will Jip pull?
answers: A big tent and a flag
The cart with Bess and her doll

lessons.title: Lesson XXV: Kate's Doll
steps: New words: James, Mary, made, sang, my, lay, sport, spade, lap, dig, doll's, sand, said; sound focus: said is a sight word

Slate work: copy “Kate made the doll's bed.”
Read the talking parts with two voices
questions: What did James want to do?
Why couldn't Kate play?

She had to make her doll's bed

lessons.title: Lesson XXVI: By the Brook
steps: New words: its, shade, brook, picks, all, by, help, stones, glad, soft; sound focus: long a (shade)
Read it once aloud for your child, then have them read it to you (or to a sibling or stuffed animal)
Slate work: copy “They are all in the shade.”
Pick up some small stones and talk about what you find
questions: Where are the children playing?
What does Mary pick up?
answers: In the shade by the brook

lessons.title: Lesson XXVII: Review: What Shall We Do?
steps: Read it as a play between Fanny and John
Slate work: copy “Shall we go to the big woods?”
Plan your own picnic: what would you take?
questions: What does John like to do?
Who will they ask to hang up a swing?
lessons.notes: Review lesson: the words at the top are old words to practice. Let your child read as independently as possible.

lessons.title: Lesson XXVIII: The Little Chick
steps: New words: peep, while, take, sleep, tuck, safe, oh, wet, feet, chick, can't, feels, wing; sound focus: ee (peep, sleep, feet)
You read a line, then your child reads it back; finish by reading the whole lesson together
Slate work: copy “Peep, peep!”
Act it out with a toy chick hiding under a 'wing'
questions: Where did the girl take the chick?
Where does the chick go to sleep?

lessons.title: Lesson XXIX: The Kite
steps: New words: wind, time, there, fence, kite, high, eyes, bright, flies, why, day, shines; sound focus: long i spelled i-e, igh, y
Let your child read the lesson aloud slowly; help only on words they can't sound out
Slate work: copy “The sun shines bright.”
Copy the slate work, then fly a kite or draw one
questions: Why does the kite fly high?
Where was the dog?
lessons.notes: Ends with slate work to copy.

lessons.title: Lesson XXX: A Boat for the Dolls
steps: New words: wish, float, tie, know, rope, boat, try, shore, give, pole, don't, push, drag, won't, oar, funny; sound focus: oa (float, boat, oar)
Read it once aloud for your child, then have them read it to you (or to a sibling or stuffed animal)
Slate work: copy “Nell let the pole fall on the tub.”
Float a small tub or bowl in water to test Kate's plan
questions: What did they use for a boat?
What happened at the end of the slate work?
answers: Nell let the pole fall and upset the tub
lessons.notes: Ends with slate work that continues the story.

lessons.title: Lesson XXXI: Brave Old Ponto
steps: New words: bound, Rose, called, got, drown, found, brave, came, Ponto, jumped, mouth, around, brought, water; sound focus: ou (bound, found, mouth)
Read the lesson aloud together, pointing to each word; then let your child read it alone
Slate work: copy “Good, old Ponto!”
Answer the question at the end: what do you think of Ponto?
questions: Who is Ponto?
Which doll did Ponto bring out first?

lessons.title: Lesson XXXII: A June Day
steps: New words: June, Lucy's, air, kind, trees, singing, blue, when, pure, says, sky, picnic; sound focus: says is a sight word
You read a line, then your child reads it back; finish by reading the whole lesson together
Slate work: copy “The sky is as blue as it can be.”
Describe the weather today the way the lesson describes June
questions: Where are Lucy and her mamma?
When will they have a picnic?
answers: When papa can get a tent

lessons.title: Lesson XXXIII: Review: The Lost Ball
steps: Read it with expression, especially the questions
Slate work: copy “Ponto has found it.”
Hide a ball and let your child find it like Ponto
questions: Who found the lost ball?
Whose feet will he lay it at?
lessons.notes: Review lesson: the words at the top are old words to practice. Let your child read as independently as possible.

lessons.title: Lesson XXXIV: The Big Flag
steps: New words: boy, our, spoil, hurrah, own, coil, noise, fourth, such, join, thank, about, hoist, pay, July, playing; sound focus: oi and oy
Read it once aloud for your child, then have them read it to you (or to a sibling or stuffed animal)
Slate work: copy “Hurrah for the flag, boys!”
Read the conversation between James and papa with two voices
questions: What were the boys playing?
What did papa give with the flag?

lessons.title: Lesson XXXV: The White Kitten
steps: New words: finished, bonnet, lesson, saved, white, away, I've, am, work, scamper, ready, garden; sound focus: two-syllable words; I've
Read the lesson aloud together, pointing to each word; then let your child read it alone
Slate work: copy “Kitty, my pretty, white kitty.”
Memorize the first four lines
questions: What has the child finished?
What did the child save for the kitty?
lessons.notes: This lesson is a script (cursive) poem. Read it together and use a stanza as copywork.

lessons.title: Lesson XXXVI: Frank's Boat
steps: New words: care, always, line, Frank, row, been, keeps, home; sound focus: ow as long o (row)
You read a line, then your child reads it back; finish by reading the whole lesson together
Slate work: copy “Frank has a pretty boat.”
Draw Frank's boat with its black line
questions: What color is Frank's boat?
Where does he keep it?
answers: White, with a black line near the water
In the pond near his home

lessons.title: Lesson XXXVII: The Little Boat
steps: New words: much, one, yet, hungry, seen, grandma, corn, would; sound focus: one is a sight word
Let your child read the lesson aloud slowly; help only on words they can't sound out
Slate work: copy “Has grandma seen it?”
Narrate: what will John give Lucy, and what is in Lucy's pan?
questions: What will John give Lucy?
What is in Lucy's pan?
answers: The little boat, when it is finished

lessons.title: Lesson XXXVIII: Going to Market
steps: New words: market, bread, basket, bought, meat, tea, trying, tell, which; sound focus: ea (bread vs. meat, tea)
Read it once aloud for your child, then have them read it to you (or to a sibling or stuffed animal)
Slate work: copy “She has bought some bread.”
Play market: 'buy' bread, meat, and tea with play money
questions: What did mamma buy?
Where are the things?
answers: In the basket on her arm

lessons.title: Lesson XXXIX: Dear Old Grandma
steps: New words: reads, so, wears, please, could, hair, fast, love, easy, gray, chair, who, glasses; sound focus: air (hair, chair)
Read the lesson aloud together, pointing to each word; then let your child read it alone
Slate work: copy “She wears glasses when she reads.”
Tell one way your child can help a grandparent
questions: What does grandma wear when she reads?
What does Robert do when she asks for a drink?
answers: Runs as fast as he can to get it

lessons.title: Lesson XL: The Bee in the Flower
steps: New words: does, wonder, mother, other, bee, honey, listen, flower; sound focus: o as short u (mother, other, honey)
You read a line, then your child reads it back; finish by reading the whole lesson together
Slate work: copy “Shall we let it out?”
Look at a real flower and find where a bee could go in
questions: What was shut up in the flower?
Why did it go into the flower?

lessons.title: Lesson XLI: Frank and James White
steps: New words: best, hitched, their, should, or, riding, live, holds, hay, driving, tight, early; sound focus: -ing endings
Let your child read the lesson aloud slowly; help only on words they can't sound out
Slate work: copy “Some horses can trot very fast.”
Copy the slate work, then talk about being kind to animals
questions: Who is riding and who is driving?
What will the boys give the horses?
answers: Frank is riding; James is driving
lessons.notes: Ends with slate work to copy.

lessons.title: Lesson XLII: The Bird's Nest

Read it once aloud for your child, then have them read it to you (or to a sibling or stuffed animal)
Slate work: copy “She left the birds.”
Narrate: what did the girl find, and why did she leave it?
questions: What was the girl looking for?
What did she find besides flowers?

lessons.title: Lesson XLIII: The Lightning Train
steps: New words: eight, ask, after, town, past, ah, ticket, right, half, two, train, ding, lightning; sound focus: eigh (eight)
Read the lesson aloud together, pointing to each word; then let your child read it alone
Slate work: copy “All right! Time is up!”
Play train in a basket or box and read it as a play
questions: What time will the train get back?
What does mamma want from town?
answers: A big basket with two good little children in it

lessons.title: Lesson XLIV: Playing School
steps: New words: school, even, three, room, small; sound focus: oo (school, room)
You read a line, then your child reads it back; finish by reading the whole lesson together
Slate work: copy “It is noon, and the school is out.”
Play school: your child is the teacher and reads to you
questions: Who is the teacher?
What is Fanny reading about?
answers: A poor little boy who was lost in the woods

lessons.title: Lesson XLV: Polly the Parrot
steps: New words: apple, mew, tease, cracker, down, new, silly, asleep, wants, calls, knew, friends, upon, flew, Poll, Polly; sound focus: ew (mew, new, knew, flew)
Let your child read the lesson aloud slowly; help only on words they can't sound out
Slate work: copy “Polly wants a cracker.”
Say Polly's lines in a parrot voice
questions: What kind of bird is Polly?
What did Polly do to tease the cat?
answers: Lit on the cat's back while she was asleep

lessons.title: Lesson XLVI: Review: A Nice Time in the Woods
steps: Read it as a conversation between mother and the child
Slate work: copy “Rab was such a good dog.”
Narrate the whole day in the woods in order
questions: Who are the best flowers for?
What did Rab guard?
lessons.notes: Review lesson: the words at the top are old words to practice. Let your child read as independently as possible.

lessons.title: Lesson XLVII: Home from the Beach
steps: New words: beach, shells, these, seat, waves, going, ever, sea, watch, evening, lazy, side; sound focus: ea (beach, seat, sea)
Read the lesson aloud together, pointing to each word; then let your child read it alone
Slate work: copy “They have been to the beach.”
If you have shells, sort them while you talk about the story
questions: What did John find?
Who is driving?

lessons.title: Lesson XLVIII: Frank Goes Fishing
steps: New words: log, quiet, proud, pulled, fish, stump, river, father; sound focus: ou (proud)
You read a line, then your child reads it back; finish by reading the whole lesson together
Slate work: copy “How proud he feels!”
Narrate: where are they, and what did Frank catch?
questions: Who took Frank fishing?
What is Frank's seat?
answers: The stump of a big tree

lessons.title: Lesson XLIX: The Rain
steps: New words: rain, outside, often, pitter, say, window, sound, patter, drops, sometimes, only, music; sound focus: compound words (outside, sometimes)
Let your child read the lesson aloud slowly; help only on words they can't sound out
Slate work: copy “Pit, pitter, patter, pat.”
Listen to rain (or a recording) and tap out the pitter-patter rhythm
questions: Where do the drops pitter-patter?
What does the child think the sound is like?
lessons.notes: This lesson is all script (cursive) slate work. Read it together first, then copy the little rhyme at the end.

lessons.title: Lesson L: Winter Fun
steps: New words: sled, throw, winter, hurt, ice, cover, Henry, next, skate, ground, merry, snow, sister, laughing, pair; sound focus: er (winter, cover, sister)
Read it once aloud for your child, then have them read it to you (or to a sibling or stuffed animal)
Slate work: copy “What fun it is to skate on the ice!”
Name your favorite winter game
questions: Why does Henry pull his sister on the sled?
How do we know the boy who fell is not hurt?
answers: She is too small to skate

lessons.title: Lesson LI: Fido's Tricks
steps: New words: paw, polite, means, isn't, speak, sir, shake, Fido, tricks, teach, dinner, Ellen, bowwow; sound focus: aw (paw)
Read the lesson aloud together, pointing to each word; then let your child read it alone
Slate work: copy “Give me your paw, Fido.”
Teach a pet or stuffed animal a 'trick' while reading
questions: What is Fido wearing?
What does Fido's 'Bowwow' mean?

lessons.title: Lesson LII: The Rat in the Shed
steps: New words: puss, shed, pain, way, stole, saw, hid, eat, Hattie, suffer, sorry, something, caught, tried, Nero; sound focus: ai, ay (pain, way)
You read a line, then your child reads it back; finish by reading the whole lesson together
Slate work: copy “Puss was hid on a big box.”
Read it as a conversation between Frank and Hattie
questions: Who caught the rat?
Why does Hattie feel sorry?
answers: She does not like to see even a rat suffer pain

lessons.title: Lesson LIII: At the Seaside
steps: New words: roll, build, grandpa, hard, foam, ships, houses, long, sail, break, wooden, blow; sound focus: oa, ai (foam, sail)
Let your child read the lesson aloud slowly; help only on words they can't sound out
Slate work: copy “They watch the waves.”
Draw a sand house with a wall around it
questions: What does grandpa like to watch?
Who are the shells for?

lessons.title: Lesson LIV: Willie's Rabbits
steps: New words: asked, wanted, four, Willie's, night, rabbits, lad, carried, cents, telling, fifty, master; sound focus: -ed endings (asked, wanted, carried)
Read it once aloud for your child, then have them read it to you (or to a sibling or stuffed animal)
Slate work: copy “What soft, kind eyes they have.”
Copy the slate work about rabbits
questions: How many rabbits did father buy?
How much did they cost?

lessons.title: Lesson LV: The Bird's Nest in the Bush
steps: New words: bush, cunning, place, show, find, broken, over, bring, again, fasten; sound focus: silent t (fasten)

Did they take the nest?

lessons.title: Lesson LVII: The Little Brown Birds

They shut, as if it were asleep

lessons.title: Lesson LXI: The Hen and Her Chickens
steps: New words: stood, himself, flapping, first, twelve, flapped, walked, flap, obey, better, Chippy, food, stone, before, chickens, kept; sound focus: -ed and -ing endings
Let your child read the lesson aloud slowly; help only on words they can't sound out
Slate work: copy “Just flap your wings.”
Act it out: jump from a 'stone' (a pillow) to the other side
questions: How many chickens did the hen have?
Where did she want to take them?

lessons.title: Lesson LXII: Chippy Tried
steps: New words: chirped, never, indeed, slowly, really, brood, began, didn't, use, door, bite, piece; sound focus: ie (piece); didn't
Read it once aloud for your child, then have them read it to you (or to a sibling or stuffed animal)
Slate work: copy “Well, I tried.”
Talk about why Chippy got the bread
questions: Who got the piece of bread?
Why?
answers: He was the only one who really tried

lessons.title: Lesson LXIII: The Last Lesson
steps: New words: last, slates, write, waste, neat, taken, clean, learn, reader, parents, second; sound focus: silent w (write)
Read the lesson aloud together, pointing to each word; then let your child read it alone
Slate work: copy “We have finished the First Reader.”
Celebrate finishing the book; look over the Phonic Chart together
questions: What book comes next?
How should children keep their books?
lessons.notes: The Phonic Chart after this lesson lists every sound taught; it makes a good review sheet.
